_warning: Phonological description only. These are linguistic annotations, not an animation specification. Rendering them is interpretation and the result is NOT validated ASL until a qualified Deaf signer reviews it.
_schema: Morpheme 1 descriptors are promoted to the top level for renderer compatibility; `morphemes` holds the full sequence (ASL-LEX codes up to six). `fidelity` is 'exact' or 'approximate'; read `mapping_note` before trusting an approximate entry.

accessible.mapping_note: ACCESS is the nearest lemma; ACCESSIBLE is not a distinct ASL-LEX entry.

assignment.mapping_note: HOMEWORK is the nearest lemma. ASSIGNMENT in a classroom register is often fingerspelled or compounded.

classroom.mapping_note: CLASS describes the group, not the room. CLASSROOM is a CLASS+ROOM compound that ASL-LEX does not code.

code.mapping_note: PROGRAM is the nearest lemma. CODE in a software sense is commonly fingerspelled.

downstairs.mapping_note: DOWN is a direction, not the STAIRS-relative locative. The real sign is directional and not captured by this lemma.

eat.mapping_note: ASL-LEX splits EAT into eat_1 and eat_2; eat_1 is used here.

everyone.mapping_note: ALL is the nearest lemma; EVERYONE is ALL+ONE-style compounding that ASL-LEX does not code.

loop.mapping_note: CIRCLE describes the path only. LOOP as a programming term has no ASL-LEX lemma and is commonly fingerspelled.

mean.mapping_note: ASL-LEX splits MEAN into mean_1 and mean_2; mean_1 is used.

question.mapping_note: Nearest single lexeme is ASK. English 'question' has no single ASL equivalent; QMwg (question-mark wiggle) differs.

represent.mapping_note: SHOW is the nearest lemma; REPRESENT is not distinctly coded.

say.mapping_note: TELL is the nearest lemma; SAY is not distinctly coded.

this.mapping_note: ASL-LEX codes this lemma as 'this/it'; the deictic use depends on real-world pointing this descriptor cannot carry.

upstairs.mapping_note: UP is a direction, not the STAIRS-relative locative.

variable.mapping_note: CHANGE is the nearest lemma. VARIABLE as a programming term has no ASL-LEX lemma and is commonly fingerspelled.

what.mapping_note: ASL-LEX splits WHAT into what_1 and what_2; what_1 is used.
